transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... well. We put in a brighter bathroom mirror recently, and... I don't know, I just keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and my jaw. It looks... uneven to me. Or kind of saggy. My husband says he can't really see what I'm talking about, but... yeah. That's why I came in.
How often do you find yourself thinking about the uneven or saggy appearance of your skin, and does it bother you a lot even when others don't notice it?

Um... I don't know. A fair amount, I guess. Like I said, it's just... ever since we put that new mirror in, I just keep noticing it. The skin there. It just looks saggy to me. And... yeah, it bothers me. Even if my husband doesn't see what I'm talking about.
How much does the appearance of your skin around the cheeks and jaw affect your daily life, such as causing distress or making you avoid certain situations?

Well... I still get my work done. It's not like I'm not doing my job. But... I guess I do spend extra time getting ready now. It's made me have to rush into the courthouse a few mornings. And... I've missed the start of my yoga class more than once. 

Um... I guess I've also stepped out of a few casual photos lately, too... like at my book club or community events. I just... I'd rather not have to worry about how my face is going to look in them. But I'm still doing my normal things, mostly.
Do you find yourself preoccupied with how your face looks, even when you’re not looking in the mirror, or do these concerns mostly come up when you're getting ready or seeing yourself in reflections?

Um... mostly when I'm getting ready, I think. I mean, most mornings I do end up checking it from a few different angles. And... I put on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse. Just to cover it. 

But... I guess it's not just at the mirror. Sometimes when I'm at work, I'll... I kind of find myself comparing my face to the other women I see around the office. And like I said before, I'll avoid being in those casual pictures if I'm just... not feeling okay about it. So... yeah.
Do you find yourself doing things like checking your face in the mirror often, using makeup to cover certain areas, or avoiding certain angles in photos because of how your face looks?

Um... yeah. Like I just said... I do check it. In the mornings, mostly. Just... making sure I look okay from different sides. And I use makeup. Just a little extra... before work. 

And... yeah, the pictures. I'd just rather not. And sometimes I... I notice other women at the office. How they look. But... that's about it.
When you’re not looking in the mirror or getting ready, do you find yourself thinking about your facial appearance frequently, such as throughout the day or during tasks like work?

Um... well, it really started when we put in this new, brighter mirror in the bathroom. That's when I... I first started noticing that the skin around my cheeks and jaw just looked... uneven. Or maybe a little saggy. 

I guess I do think about it sometimes during the day. Even though my husband says he doesn't really see what I'm talking about... I just... I know it's there. So, yes, it crosses my mind.
Have there been times when your concern about the way your face looks has caused you a lot of distress, or made it hard for you to focus on other things like your work or time with family?

Um... I wouldn't really say a lot of distress. I still get my work done just fine. 

But... I guess the extra time I spend getting ready in the mornings... it has made me have to rush into the courthouse a few times. And... I've missed the start of my yoga class more than once because of it. 

And... like I mentioned before about pictures, I have skipped being in a few casual ones at my book club... and some community events. I just... I didn't want to worry about how my face would look in them. But... I still do my normal things, mostly.
Do you believe that the saggy or uneven appearance of your skin is something that should be obvious to others, even if they don't seem to notice it when you point it out?

Um... well. I mean, yes. I see it. It's... it's right there. Like I said, when we put in that brighter mirror, it just... became obvious to me. The unevenness. The way it sags around my jaw. 

My husband... he says he doesn't see it. But... I don't know how he couldn't. I mean, I see it. So... yes, I think it's there. Even if he doesn't.
Do you believe that the way your cheeks and jaw look is a defect that others should notice, even if they tell you they don't see it?
Um... I thought I just answered that. I mean... yes. Like I said, I see it, so I think it's there. I don't really know what else to tell you.
Do you think your concern about the sagging skin around your cheeks and jaw is excessive, or do you feel like it's a reasonable thing to be worried about?
Um... I don't know. I guess... I think it's reasonable. I mean, it's my face. Anyone would care about that. I wouldn't call it excessive.

Do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors, like checking your face in the mirror, applying makeup to hide the area, or avoiding certain angles in photos, because of your concerns about your facial appearance?

Well... I guess so. Most mornings, before I leave for the courthouse, I do check my face from a few different angles. And... I put on a little extra makeup. Just to be careful. 

Sometimes at work, I might compare myself to the other women there. And I'd rather avoid casual pictures if I'm... if I'm not feeling okay about how I look that day. But I just do what I have to do.
Do you feel like you have to check your face in the mirror or apply makeup in a certain way, even if you know it might not be necessary?

Um... I think I just went over this. But... yes. Like I said, before I head to the courthouse, I check my face from those angles and put on the makeup. I don't really think about whether it's necessary or not... I just feel like I need to do it. And... like I mentioned, comparing myself to the other women at work, or staying out of pictures when I feel bad... it's just what I do. I don't really have much else to add to that.

Do you feel that you have to perform specific behaviors, like checking your face in the mirror or applying makeup in a certain way, to reduce the anxiety or discomfort you feel about how your cheeks and jaw look?

Look, I... we literally just went over this. But, yes. Doing those things... checking my face from a few angles, putting on the extra makeup before I go to the courthouse... it just makes me feel a little less uncomfortable, I guess. And... like I just said, comparing myself to the women at work, or avoiding those casual pictures... it's just how I handle it when I'm not feeling okay about my face. That's... that's really all there is to it.

Do you feel that you have to perform certain routines, like checking your face in the mirror or applying makeup a specific way, to try to reduce the discomfort you feel about how your cheeks and jaw look?

I... I really don't know what else to say about this. We keep going in circles. 

Yes. Like I've said every time... I check my face from a few angles, I put on the extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse... and I compare myself to the women at work, or just stay out of casual pictures if I'm not feeling okay about it. I do it to deal with the discomfort, yes. I really don't have another way to explain it. Can we please move on to something else?

Have you ever felt that the way your face looks is so unattractive or abnormal that you’ve had trouble thinking about anything else, or has it ever made it hard for you to function normally in your day-to-day life?

I mean... I can still function fine. I always get my work done. It's not like I can't do my job. 

I guess... the extra time I spend getting ready does mean I end up rushing into the courthouse some mornings. And... I've missed the start of my yoga class a few times because of it. Um, and like I mentioned before about pictures, I just... I skip being in casual photos at my book club or community events. It's just easier than worrying about how my face is going to look. But... I still do my day-to-day stuff.

candidates: L98.9 Disorder of skin and subcutaneous tissue, unspecified
F32.9 Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
inference_history.note: The patient presents with concerns about physical appearance (skin around cheeks and jaw appearing uneven or saggy), which may indicate body dysmorphic disorder. There is also a need to rule out dermatological causes and assess for anxiety or depressive symptoms that may be contributing to or resulting from the concern.
Ruled out L98.9 (skin condition not otherwise specified) as the concern is more psychological in nature and related to appearance preoccupation rather than a primary dermatological issue.

The patient's belief that the perceived facial flaw should be obvious to others, despite their lack of confirmation, supports F45.22 (Body Dysmorphic Disorder). However, absence of severe distress or significant functional impairment makes F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, unspecified) less likely. F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) remains due to ongoing worries about appearance, though less central.
